ClientResponses.Response: Hi, and thanks for sharing your experience with the Traeger Timberline. Even though the basic functionality of most pellet grills is the same, there are a few things to get used to when going from the original style Traeger to something as new and advanced as the Timberline. While maintenance is certainly the single most common cause of grill fires on any type of outdoor grill, this doesn’t appear to be the case in your situation. With this eliminated, there’s only a few other possible reasons that fires might occur. One of them is putting aluminum foil or a liner on the drip tray. Due to the way that the new EZ Clean trays are designed, they do not require any kind of protective covering, while still being very easy to maintain, and using one can certainly result in a grill overheating, or on rare occasions, a grill fire. Another possibility is that the firepot is not completely seated at the bottom of the grill, with the right lip caught on the lower edge of the auger tube. This may cause the pellets to collect beneath the pot, where they can eventually ignite, creating more heat than expected. Additionally, if the grill did not go through the full shutdown on a previous cook, there could be excess pellets remaining in the firepot for the next run, creating a larger fire than usual. But as opposed to trying to work this out by yourself, please give Traeger Customer Service a call for assistance. One of our agents can check over everything with you, and maybe do a test run as well, likely having the grill working perfectly by the time you get off the phone.

I don’t know what’s going on with that, but I refuse to call in just to be connected to someone overseas. That’s right, Traeger outsources its call center. Traeger claims that all the ash from the burn pot is supposed to blow into the drip bucket, it does not. In fact, there is very little ash in there. I should have reviewed more high end smokers before purchasing to see what I was missing out on, but where I live, we only have big box stores. ClientResponses.Response: Hi, and thank you for reviewing the Timberline XL. Typically, if a grill loses a connection that it had previously maintained then it should simply come down to finding what was changed. Either there was something externally that affected its access to the network, or possibly a change with the grill itself. As for the potential external causes, this is usually related to some modification of the WiFi or phone that the grill was paired to. But regarding the latter, you can easily verify this by trying a different compatible device and seeing if you get the same results. On the grill side, anytime your Traeger drops the connection you’ll always want to go through the Forget Network steps first before trying to reconnect. For the new touchscreen models like the Timberline XL, this is done by going to the Main Menu and selecting WiFIRE connectivity > WiFi Info > Forget Network > Yes. Once done, try the pairing process again. In reference to the temperature and pellet use, for this to occur suddenly after working ok previously is usually indicative of a problem with the pellets. Compromised pellets are the #1 cause of temperature issues, and can be the result moisture absorption, or even dust buildup in the bottom of the hopper. A quick verification or pellet quality is breaking a few between your fingers to see if they either easily crumble apart, break cleanly in half, or something in-between. If it is anything other than a clean break, you may want to try new pellets. But if the above steps don’t work, or you would simply like some help with going through them, please give us a call at the Traeger support line. Not only can one of our agents assist with connecting the grill, but they can also see why your temperature performance has changed and help get it back running the way it should be.

I bought this same grill from a local authorized dealer, which was a great experience. However, I have to say that my immediate experience with the grill itself was very disappointing. I set out to season the grill as recommended and later cook four racks of ribs according to Traeger’s 3-2-1 recipe. Everything looked great according to the perceived temps. I’ve cooked this same recipe on a competitors wood fired grill and it was on the money, so I naturally thought with the Traeger Timberline XL the cook would be even better. Unfortunately, it was one of the worst cooks I’ve ever done. I knew something was up when I grabbed the ribs from the 2-hour shift and didn’t witness ANY bone separation, but I continued the cook as directed. To note, I did make the mistake of just following the recipe, but I can assure you the grill was the main problem. I finally got the ribs on the plate and when we bit in…the ribs were raw closest to the bone. Apparently, the perceived ambient temp of the grill was off by some 50 degrees. So, instead of it sitting at 225 for two hours regarding one part of the cook, it actually sat at 175. I only realized this afterwards when I tested another cook of Pork Ribs with a third party remote thermometer. This thermometer broke the case wide open when it read the ambient temp at minus 50 degrees of the registered temperature reading on the grill. 

Working with customer service proved to be a waste of time since they determined that the grill needed a new thermocouple, which required me to disassemble the grill that was a week old. Not exactly ideal. I would later speak to the regional sales manager, and he assured me the local authorized dealer would send one of their associates to install the thermocouple. Well, at a $4,000+ price tag considering tax, you would think the company had enough to pay a certified tech to stop out and perform additional tests. To say the least, the thermocouple DID NOT fix the grill temperature issue. Moreover, the sales manager assured me that he would not allow Traeger’s customer support to start “parting” me to death. His words were, and I quote, “I will only throw one part at a grill, and if it doesn’t work we’ll replace it all together.” So much for that, the first thing he did was ignore my subsequent calls to identify the part didn’t work, and would later claim that any third party thermometer should not be trusted; however, Traeger has actually bought that very same technology from the third party thermometer company and have incorporated their tech into the new Traeger wireless thermometer system. Go figure! Either way, I eventually elected to return the grill to the local authorized dealer, which was a chore in and of itself. Regardless, I’m happier without the headache wondering if my next cook would be ruined. Essentially, I had to cook some chicken in the old pellet grill because the Traeger just didn’t get to temp as expected. 

Be weary of this product line. Period.

Traegers, like other smokers, cook on an average temperature, so we can expect some variation due to the nature of how they work. While in use, temperatures are shown in real-time, which can result in a variance of +/- 25-degrees, but the average will be very close to what the grill is set to.

ClientResponses.Response:
Hey Nelrock,

Thanks for taking the time to review your Traeger app! 5 GHz WiFi connections are very bad at transmitting through walls compared to 2.4 GHz signals. Since our grills do not require fast download speeds, but are expected to stay connected while separated from its router by your home's external walls, we opted to only use the better connection option in our grill's situation.

While the grill needs to connect via 2.4 GHz, your device with the Traeger app can be on any internet connection after the pairing process is done and still communicate with the grill. This allows you to keep on eye on temps all over the home as you go about your day, or even while on your mobile data!

Please don't hesitate to reach out to our Support team with any questions or concerns, we're always happy to help our Traegerhood.

Results.ReviewText:
Bought grill in May 2022. After a couple uses, igniter went out. Took about a month to get replacement. So, rough start. The grill, when it runs, is outstanding. The wifire part though and the app, not so much.
Have had intermittent grill connection with the app from the start. Updates fail.
So, after a number of calls I was informed that the grill has to connect to the app in order to update. Since I was having issues with the app...no update.
I was told that the grill only uses 2.4ghz wifi. This, I knew, was a part of the documentation. What they don't tell you is if the app is on a device which can also use 5ghz...like, oh...every device in 2022, now 2023, you will have the problems I was having. Despite being on the same network, the grill and app have issues.
The solution I was given was that I had to split my wifi bands into separate SSID's (wifi network names). One for 2.4, one for 5. When I wanted to use the grill, I need to switch the device with the app to the 2.4 network name. Devices which can use either band, I now have to force them to use one or the other.
So, I don't know which to blame here, the app or the grill only capable of 2.4ghz, but, my phone ran about $1200. It can use 5 or 2.4. My $4000+, modern...less than year old...grill/app can't. To me, the app should be able to handle to device being on the same network as the grill, regardless of what band either is connected to, but my expertise here is 0, so...
In any case...grill cooks fantastically. The wifire/app though could use some work.

My last review was 15 days ago when they sent me a new fix, the hopper assemble. After receiving it it looked easy on the video to install but the video does not show all the steps to remove and replace the hopper and there has been always one screw the strips so you have to remove that problem as well. One and a half hours later i got it close to installed but did not work I had one wire that i didnt know where it went and the video does not show you how or where they go. Called service TWO HOUR WAIT. So I decided to call the next day and spoke to a tech and  we finally got it installed but it was the same problem that I originally called in on in Oct.
She said she would escalate it to and should have an answer on Tues because Monday was a holiday. Call on Tuesday spoke with another tech he had me get it online and update the software and run a diagnosis and still had same two faults as in OCT.
He said he would have an answer in 24 hours and to call and they would have a resolution to the problem. I received  an email with a new case number and instructions to call in 24 hours and the would have a resolution to my problem. I thought Great i finally going to get a fix to the problem after 3 months. Called today 24 hours later as email stated gave my case number new tech said, No it could take 3 to 5 business days or when ever the engineers get to look at it, so it could take longer.
I asked if i should call every day to find out if they got a resolution and he said no they would call me. The last Tech told me after another promise to call within 24hours that Traeger does not promise to call anyone back. Now i am confused I have a $3700 broken grill that i got to use 2 months and have no idea when or if it will ever work. 
I have spent hours working on this grill and have replace every part that they have sent.
I would not buy this grill unless you have the skill set, the time and the tools and want to make your life miserable.
